name: C2f (CSP bottleneck with two convolutions, faster)

whatIsIt.eli5: A team of helpers. Half of the notes skip ahead untouched, the other half go through several helpers in a row, and at the end everyone's notes are put together.
whatIsIt.simple: YOLOv8's main feature block. It splits the map into two halves, sends one half through a chain of small Bottleneck blocks, keeps the output of every step, and joins everything back together with a final 1×1 Conv.
whatIsIt.engineer: Cross-Stage-Partial variant: cv1 (1×1) to 2c channels → chunk into two c-channel parts → n Bottlenecks applied sequentially to the second part → concat [part1, part2, b1…bn] ((2+n)·c channels) → cv2 (1×1) to c2.

whyExists.eli5: Keeping some notes untouched and saving every helper's work means nothing important gets lost, and it is cheaper than making everyone redo the whole job.
whyExists.simple: Only half of the channels go through the expensive bottlenecks, which saves compute. Keeping every intermediate output gives the next layer a mix of shallow and deeper views and gives training many short paths for the learning signal.
whyExists.engineer: Partial processing reduces FLOPs; dense aggregation of intermediate outputs (ELAN-like) enriches gradient flow and receptive-field diversity compared with C3, where only the last bottleneck output is concatenated.

eli5: A first helper rewrites the notes.
The notes are cut into two piles.
One pile goes through a line of helpers; each helper's copy is kept.
All the piles are stacked together.
A last helper summarizes the stack.
simple: cv1: a 1×1 Conv makes 2c channels (c is half of the block's output width).
The result is split into two parts of c channels each.
The second part goes through n Bottleneck blocks one after another; each Bottleneck's output is saved.
All parts are joined: 2 + n pieces of c channels each.
cv2: a 1×1 Conv mixes them back down to the output width.
engineer: Each Bottleneck: 3×3 → 3×3 Conv with e = 1.0 and an optional residual add (shortcut=True in the backbone, False in the neck).
Repeats n are scaled by depth_multiple: n = max(round(n·d), 1).

example.eli5: In YOLOv8n layer 4, 64 layers of notes come in; 32 go through 2 helpers, and at the end 4 piles of 32 are joined and squeezed back to 64.
example.simple: YOLOv8n layer 4: input and output 64 channels, n = 2 (the YAML says 6, times depth 0.33 → 2). c = 32. cv1 makes 64 channels, split into 32 + 32; two Bottlenecks run on the second half; the join has (2 + 2) × 32 = 128 channels; cv2 brings it back to 64. Total 49,664 parameters.

typicalPositions.eli5: After each step where the picture gets smaller, and in the mixing part.
typicalPositions.simple: In YOLOv8 after every stride-2 Conv in the backbone (with shortcut) and after every Concat in the neck (without shortcut).
typicalPositions.engineer: Backbone stages (shortcut=True) and every PAN-FPN fusion node (shortcut=False) in YOLOv8.

tradeoffs.eli5: More helpers in the line see more, but are slower.
tradeoffs.simple: More repeats (n) increase what the block can learn and its field of view but add cost linearly. The join grows with n, so cv2 gets bigger too.
tradeoffs.engineer: Params/FLOPs grow ~linearly in n; the concat width (2+n)·c increases cv2 cost; memory traffic from keeping all intermediates is higher than C3.
